Legacy Heart Songs™

You bring the heartbeat. | We'll make it sing.

Hi — I’m Peter. For years I’ve been finding unique ways to celebrate the people we love. It’s one of my favorite things to do!

We capture a real heartbeat and set it to music performed by real musicians, creating a meaningful experience for loved ones to share and a one-of-a-kind keepsake you can hold in your hands and treasure for years to come.

The experience

First, make the recording.

Sit close, put the stethoscope to their chest, find the beat, listen, and record. Capture the moment with a photo, and one of our musicians sets it to music so you can come back to it for years.

We’ll make you two files: your authentic heartbeat or voice, optimized for quality, and one with gentle music for an atmosphere of remembering.

How it works

Five steps, and we walk you through every one.

Video coming soon How to make a heartbeat recording
1

Tell us who, and when

Use the form to tell us who you’d like to record, any date you’re working toward, and whether you’d like a keepsake to hold.

We’ll write back with a PayPal link or a Venmo request, and a timeline — when the recording kit will reach you, and our best estimate of when you’ll receive the finished song.

2

Capture the sound in a moment that means something

We mail you a recording kit with the postage already paid, both ways, and a card that shows you exactly how to do the recording. Gather whoever you’d like to be there.

In the Philadelphia area it may be possible for us to come and do it in person.

3

Send it back

Email the recording to studio@legacyheartsongs.com using the instructions in the kit, then drop the kit in the prepaid envelope.

Emailing the file is the surest way to get it to us safely — but if that isn't your thing, just send the kit back and we'll do it for you.

4

A musician goes to work

We gently refine the recording for clarity while preserving the natural sound of the heartbeat, then arrange music around it so the heartbeat remains the heart of the song.

5

It arrives

Two files in your inbox — the song, and the heartbeat on its own — and your keepsake in your hands, if you chose one. Something to play at a birthday, an anniversary, or on a quiet afternoon, for as many years as you want it.

The process takes about three to four weeks, start to finish. We have a limited number of kits, so we'll tell you the current wait before you pay.

Our musicians

Every note is played by one of us — three generations of us.

Nothing here is generated. We don't use AI for music composition. Sometimes the strings are a keyboard — but a person is playing them, one note at a time. And a person listens to every piece before it leaves.

Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

For our detail people.

If your question isn't answered, write to us and we'll get back to you.

What does it cost?

$240 for The HeartSong by Email. That covers the recording kit mailed to your door, the postage both ways, the engineering, the music, and both audio files.

$285 if you'd also like a keepsake to hold: The HeartSong Portrait.

If you already have a recording and send it to us yourself, take $60 off either: $180 or $225. No kit goes out, and that $60 is what covers the equipment — its wear, loss and replacement — and the round-trip postage.

How do I pay?

Tell us what you'd like on the start-the-process page. We'll get back to you as soon as we can, with the current wait for a kit and a PayPal link — or a Venmo request instead, if you'd rather.

We ask for the whole amount at the start rather than chasing you for a balance later. We'd rather the last thing you hear from us be the music.

Nothing is charged until you've seen the wait time and said yes.

What if I need to cancel?

Before the kit goes in the mail, we refund everything, no questions and no awkwardness.

Once the kit has been mailed, we refund everything except the $60 that covers the equipment and the postage, as soon as the kit is back with us. Send it back in the prepaid envelope and we'll take care of the rest.

What's in the recording kit — and why is there sometimes a wait?

It isn't an ordinary stethoscope. Ours is customized so you can listen and record at the same time. The microphone inside is specialized too: its range reaches down into the low frequencies where a heartbeat actually lives, which most microphones miss. And the recorder has a quality preamp built in, so what it captures is clean from the start.

All of that means a single kit costs us nearly as much as a whole order. We keep a small number in circulation, which is why you may sometimes wait for one — and why we always tell you how long before you pay.

Did you change my person's heartbeat?

A little, and here's exactly what we did.

Most hearts don't land on a musical tempo. Yours was probably a few beats off from the song you chose, so we nudged the speed — usually by a few percent — until the two agreed.

We also cleaned the recording up: took out the rumble underneath, along with the sounds of clothing and movement. Then we looped the steadiest passages we could find, so the beat holds even and unbroken all the way through the song.

What we didn't do is replace anything or generate anything, so the sound you sent is the sound that gets sent back. The second file we send you is the heartbeat at its exact original speed, so you have that too.

Is any of this made by AI?

No. Every note is performed by one of us, in real time. Sometimes a flute or a string section is a keyboard patch — but a person is playing it, making choices about timing and touch.

How do I make a good recording?

The card in the kit walks you through it, but here is the whole of it:

  • The hardest part is getting the room as quiet as possible. Go to a quieter room if you can. Turn off the dishwasher and the television. Listen for the refrigerator — it's a low hum you stop noticing, and you can unplug it for a few minutes (don't forget to plug it back in!). Listen for fans, traffic, sirens and for dogs.
  • Make three separate recordings, about thirty seconds each. Make sure to make lots of jokes between each one :-)
  • Ask your person to breathe evenly and as quietly as they can.
  • Hold the stethoscope still. Light pressure, not too firm.

Once the three recordings are saved, and if you can, move the files to a computer with the USB cord in the kit and email them to us. That gets us working sooner and means the recordings won't get lost in the mail. You may need to send one file per email, since they're large. And if transferring files isn't your thing, say so — we'll pull them off the recorder when the kit comes back, and it's no trouble at all.

What if the recording doesn't come out?

The best thing is to email the recording to us so we can verify that it came out ok before posting the kit back to us. If that doesn't work out, write to studio@legacyheartsongs.com and we'll fix it. If there's still time, we'll send a second kit at no charge. If there isn't — and sometimes there isn't — we'll talk it through with you honestly and find the right thing to do, which may be a refund.

Some chests are harder to record than others, and it isn't your fault when one is. If you tell us up front who we're recording, we can often steer you to the setup most likely to work the first time.

What exactly arrives, and on what?

Two audio files, always: the song, and the heartbeat on its own at its true speed.

They come to your inbox. If you chose the Portrait, its QR badge opens them too: scan it with a phone camera to play or download either file.

Even so: please save a copy somewhere else. Download it, put it in a cloud folder, give a copy to one other person in the family. This is the one file you can't remake.

How should I listen to it?

On a Bluetooth speaker or a stereo, not a phone. The difference is not subtle — a heartbeat lives at the very bottom of what a speaker can reproduce, and a phone speaker simply cannot get down there, so you may not be able to hear the beat at all on a phone or laptop speaker.

Hold the speaker in your hands while it plays, if you can. You'll feel the beat as well as hear it, and that turns out to be the part people remember.

Can I record a baby, or a pet?

Pets, absolutely!

Babies and animals have much faster hearts, so rather than dragging the music up to meet them, we usually let the beat fall on the off-beats — it sits inside the groove instead of fighting it. It sounds right, and it's still exactly their heart.

One thing we don't do: fetal heartbeats recorded on a home doppler. That's a different legal world and we stay out of it.

Can I share it?

Yes. Send it to every cousin, play it at the service, put it on a phone for someone who can't travel. The song is yours.

Is the music licensed?

Yes. \1

Your heartbeat is a different matter: it's yours, and we don't use it for anything except your own order and to get better at working with this kind of sound.

How will my medical data be kept private?

A recording is never put into an AI tool or an online database with a name attached to it. We don't sell it, we don't share it, and we don't hand it to anyone for research.

We use it to make what you ordered, and to keep getting better at handling this kind of sound — never attached to a name. Sending us a recording is your consent for that.

We absolutely value the privacy of your medical data.

Is this medical in any way?

No, and we want to be very clear about it. A heart song is a keepsake. It is not a medical device, it doesn't detect or diagnose anything, and nothing about how it sounds tells you anything about anyone's health. Please don't read it that way, and please talk to a doctor about anything medical.

Can I talk to an actual person first?

Yes, and we'd rather you did. Write to info@legacyheartsongs.com and tell us as much or as little as you want. We answer every email ourselves, and we'll come back to you as soon as we can.

There is no deadline on our end, no hold on a kit that expires, and nobody will follow up to pressure you. If you write once and then don't write again for six months, that's completely fine.

More is coming here: printable instruction sheets for the recording kit, and short videos showing how to get a clean recording with the equipment in the bag.

While they're still here to hear it.

The best time to record a heartbeat is an ordinary afternoon, with nothing wrong. If that's where you are, start there.

Here's what happens after you send this

  1. We write back with the current wait for a kit, and a PayPal link — or a Venmo request instead, if you'd prefer.
  2. Once you've paid, the recording kit is usually with you within the week, with a card showing exactly what to do and prepaid postage home.
  3. Then the part that matters: choose a quiet moment, gather whoever you'd like, and listen to their heart together while you record. Afterwards, email the files to studio@legacyheartsongs.com and drop the kit in the envelope.
  4. Three to four weeks later, your song arrives — and your keepsake, if you chose one.
